verdict.rationale: Aider is itself a built-in AI coding assistant. Its docs show users handing it natural-language tasks in chat, and it can work out which files need editing on its own. It can run one-shot instructions with --message, take tasks from #AI comments in watch mode, use architect/editor mode, take voice requests, and auto-run tests after edits. Community users confirm it delivers on delegated coding tasks. Missing for 10: a first-party autonomous multi-step agent mode (the navigator/autonomy mode is a community add-on), and evidence of consistent output reliability, since users report subtle errors.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can delegate tasks to a built-in AI assistant inside the product

citations.quote: You can use aider without adding any files, and it will try to figure out which files need to be edited based on your requests.
Aider takes a `--message` argument, where you can give it a natural language instruction. It will do that one thing, apply the edits to the files and then exit.
AI! triggers aider to make changes to your code.
Request new features, test cases or bug fixes using your voice and let aider do the work of editing the files in your local git repo.
Then Aider delivered from the first prompt.
